authorization: The user requested an autonomous OpenClaw platform supervisor for jumpserve-front-end, jumpserve-back-end and jumpserve-infra, explicitly including automatic merge and production deployment plus private remote progress and controls.
acceptance: Verified Google platform operators alone can read the dashboard, queue work, pause/resume admission, cancel queued work and disable automatic releases; arbitrary signed-in users cannot self-enroll.
Tasks, original model requests/responses, events, changes, operations, release verification and artifact identities persist separately from research assessment records.
An externally enforced worker lease, cancellation, deadline, conservative reservation ledger and fixed repository/release scope survive restarts. Missing costs remain unknown.
OpenClaw edits isolated source copies without deployment credentials. Trusted code freezes changes, runs required checks and publishes only matching tested contents.
Exact PR head and up-to-date protected-base checks precede automatic merges. Every external mutation has a durable intent; uncertain outcomes are reconciled without blind replay.
Release workflows address explicit components and exact revisions. Broad push-to-main deployments cannot run in parallel with the supervisor release path.
Completion requires recorded production verification of the released revision; submitted workflows and successful merges are separate states.
Private desktop/mobile UI exposes recorded stages, failures, evidence, PRs, release versions and controls, including empty, denied and unavailable states.

Actual isolated SQL, sandbox coding, GitHub/AWS protocol fixtures, restart/failure injection and browser checks preserve unsuccessful trials. Fixtures do not imply live deployment or independent validation.
bootstrap: New service credentials, operator enrollment and initial production installation must be verified explicitly. The supervisor's standing authority does not grant unrelated interactive sessions blanket deployment permission.
